description: Check a place before searching with it: the canonical name, location_id, centre and radius of a town, city, county, region, country, outcode or postcode, or a 404.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
**A place name, postcode or outcode to resolve.** Required; 1 - 120 characters; case-insensitive.

Towns, cities, counties, regions, countries, districts, outcodes and full postcodes resolve (`leeds` → `Leeds`, id 1120;
`LS1`; `ls11ur` → `LS1 1UR`; `W1A 0AX` → its outcode `W1A`), spelt as `/location-suggestions` spells them or without
their punctuation (`St Albans` → "St. Albans", `Saint Neots` → "St. Neots", `Stoke on Trent` → "Stoke-on-Trent",
`Tyne & Wear` → "Tyne and Wear"), with a county, council area or country, with or without the comma (`Leeds, West
Yorkshire`, `Perth, Scotland`, `Hamilton, South Lanarkshire`, `Wellington Shropshire` → "Wellington, Telford"), or by another
name of the place (`Newham` → "Newham (London Borough)", `Staines` → "Staines-upon-Thames", `Herts` → "Hertfordshire").
A name several places share resolves when the job search reads it as one of them and that one is the main
place of the name  -  a town (`Burton` → "Burton-on-Trent", `Southend` → "Southend-on-Sea") or the one with most of
the jobs (`Richmond` → "Richmond, Surrey"); otherwise it is a 404 listing them (`Yorkshire`, `Mile End`, `St Ives`).
Ex: `Leeds`, `Saint Neots`, `Newham`, `W1A 0AX`.

description: The job sectors with their roles  -  the sector_id values every job search filters by.

Search UK job adverts with every filter (place and radius, sector, salary, contract, hours, remote, posting date) and get job records with plain-text descriptions, salaries and coordinates, 25 per page.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description:
**Free-text search over job titles and descriptions  -  the site's own search box.** Optional; omit to match every job.

**Matching:** Words separated by spaces must all match (`nurse midwife`); a comma means ANY of the terms (`nurse, midwife` returns jobs matching either); double quotes match an exact phrase (`"registered nurse"`).

**Exclusions & operators:** `-word` or `NOT word` excludes (`developer -java`); `-( … )` / `NOT ( … )` excludes a group (`nurse -(midwife OR doctor)`). `OR` / `|` / `/` / `and/or` means either word (`nurse OR midwife` = `nurse/midwife`); a `/` before an exclusion does not, so `tiler/-roofer` = `tiler -roofer`. `AND` requires both terms, and parentheses group expressions (`(developer OR engineer) AND python`).

**Wildcards & special characters:** `*` / `?` are wildcards (`develop*`). There are no boosts: `^` is read as a space (`nurse^2` searches `nurse 2`), and `%` is also read as a space (`100% remote` searches `100 remote`). Exception: a `%` between a word and a hyphen is dropped so the hyphen stays one (`20%-30%` = `20-30`, not `20 -30`).

**Other rules:** A value with no word at all  -  only punctuation or operators such as `,`, `|`, `OR`, `and/or`  -  is refused with a 400. A curly apostrophe is read as a straight one (`children’s nurse` = `children's nurse`).

**Examples:** `software developer`, `nurse, midwife`, `"data analyst"`, `developer -java`. **Up to 200 characters.**

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
**Where the job is  -  a UK town, city, district, county, region, country or postcode, or up to 5 places separated by
`;`.** Optional; omit to search the whole UK.

Take the spelling from `/location-suggestions`; `/resolve-location` shows the exact place a text searches and explains
any refusal in full. Ex: `Leeds`, `Leeds; Manchester`, `SW1A 1AA`.

- **Other spellings** read as the listed place (`Herts` → "Hertfordshire"); a shared name is its main town (`Burton` →
  "Burton-on-Trent"); a postcode searches its outcode.
- **Town + area**, with or without the comma: a county, council area or nation narrows the town
  (`Leeds, West Yorkshire`, `Belfast, NI`); abbreviations and compass prefixes work (`Livingston, W Lothian`).
- **Postal county:** a town sent with a county other than its postal county is refused with a 400 naming the postal
  county (`Coventry, Warwickshire` → West Midlands).
- A town outside the area named is refused with a 400 (`Maidstone, East Sussex`).

**Several places:** `Leeds; London` matches jobs in ANY of them, each within `distance_miles`, each job counted once.
A comma or `&` cannot separate places  -  `Leeds, London` is refused with a 400 asking for `;`.

**Home working:** `Remote`, `WFH`, `Work from home`, `Working from home` or `Home based` searches fully remote UK jobs,
on its own only  -  not in a `;` list, with `distance_miles` or with a `remote_working` other than `remote`. For remote
jobs in a place, send the place with `remote_working=remote`.

**Refusals** name what to send  -  never a silent search elsewhere: a shared name that is not the main place (candidates
listed), a name read as another place, or no such place (`UK`, `QQ9`). A real place with no matching job answers 0;
nationwide adverts can appear in any place search (`exclude_survey_jobs=true` drops the paid-survey ones).

**Echo:** `locations_resolved` lists each place (`query`, `location_id`, the `name` searched, and `exact_match`  -  `false`
when the text stood for it under another name); `location_resolved` is the first, null for home working.

parameters.name: distance_miles
parameters.description:
**Search radius around `location`, in miles.** Optional; default `10`; range `0` - `50`; needs `location`.

`0` keeps jobs in the place itself. The website offers 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 50; any whole number in the range works.
50 miles is the widest radius (a larger one returns exactly the 50-mile result, so it is refused).

parameters.name: min_salary
parameters.description:
**Salary floor, in pounds, in the unit set by `salary_unit` (annual by default).** Optional; `0` or more; pence allowed
(up to 2 decimal places, e.g. `12.21` with `salary_unit=hourly`).

Keeps jobs whose pay range REACHES the floor  -  the top of the range counts, so a £30,000 - £40,000 job passes
`min_salary=40000`. Pay is compared ANNUALISED, so hourly and daily-rate jobs are included on equal terms (a £500/day
contract passes `min_salary=40000`). Jobs that hide their pay ("Competitive salary") are matched on an undisclosed
figure the employer entered (not published: their `salary.from` / `to` are null), so some pass a floor their advert
does not show; add `salary_shown_only=true` to drop them. Ex: `30000`, `12.21` with `salary_unit=hourly`, or `500` with
`salary_unit=daily`.

parameters.name: salary_unit
parameters.description:
**The unit `min_salary` / `max_salary` are written in.** Optional; `annual` when omitted. Send it only with
`min_salary` or `max_salary`  -  on its own it is refused with a 400.

- `annual`  -  pounds per year (`30000`)
- `hourly`  -  pounds per hour (`15`; × 1,950 = 37.5 hours × 52 weeks, so `20` = `39000` a year)
- `daily`  -  pounds per day (`500`; × 260 working days, so `500` = `130000` a year)
- `weekly`  -  pounds per week (`1000`; × 52)
- `monthly`  -  pounds per month (`5000`; × 12)

The bounds are converted to annual pay with exactly these factors  -  `min_salary=20&salary_unit=hourly` returns the
same jobs as `min_salary=39000`. It changes how the bounds are read, not which jobs qualify by pay type: hourly,
daily and annual adverts are all compared on annualised pay either way.

parameters.description:
**Only jobs first posted on or after this moment.** Optional; a date (`2026-09-20`, midnight UTC) or an ISO date-time
(`2026-09-20T09:00:00Z`; a time without a zone is read as UTC; an offset such as `+01:00` is honoured). A future

its `created_at` does not). For "how many new since X" without rows, send it to `/search-jobs` with `page_size=1` and
read `total_results`.

keywords.description:
**Free-text search over job titles and descriptions  -  the site's own search box.** Optional; omit to match every job.

**Matching:** Words separated by spaces must all match (`nurse midwife`); a comma means ANY of the terms (`nurse, midwife` returns jobs matching either); double quotes match an exact phrase (`"registered nurse"`).

**Exclusions & operators:** `-word` or `NOT word` excludes (`developer -java`); `-( … )` / `NOT ( … )` excludes a group (`nurse -(midwife OR doctor)`). `OR` / `|` / `/` / `and/or` means either word (`nurse OR midwife` = `nurse/midwife`); a `/` before an exclusion does not, so `tiler/-roofer` = `tiler -roofer`. `AND` requires both terms, and parentheses group expressions (`(developer OR engineer) AND python`).

**Wildcards & special characters:** `*` / `?` are wildcards (`develop*`). There are no boosts: `^` is read as a space (`nurse^2` searches `nurse 2`), and `%` is also read as a space (`100% remote` searches `100 remote`). Exception: a `%` between a word and a hyphen is dropped so the hyphen stays one (`20%-30%` = `20-30`, not `20 -30`).

**Other rules:** A value with no word at all  -  only punctuation or operators such as `,`, `|`, `OR`, `and/or`  -  is refused with a 400. A curly apostrophe is read as a straight one (`children’s nurse` = `children's nurse`).

**Examples:** `software developer`, `nurse, midwife`, `"data analyst"`, `developer -java`. **Up to 200 characters.**

location.description:
**Where the job is  -  a UK town, city, district, county, region, country or postcode, or up to 5 places separated by
`;`.** Optional; omit to search the whole UK.

Take the spelling from `/location-suggestions`; `/resolve-location` shows the exact place a text searches and explains
any refusal in full. Ex: `Leeds`, `Leeds; Manchester`, `SW1A 1AA`.

- **Other spellings** read as the listed place (`Herts` → "Hertfordshire"); a shared name is its main town (`Burton` →
  "Burton-on-Trent"); a postcode searches its outcode.
- **Town + area**, with or without the comma: a county, council area or nation narrows the town
  (`Leeds, West Yorkshire`, `Belfast, NI`); abbreviations and compass prefixes work (`Livingston, W Lothian`).
- **Postal county:** a town sent with a county other than its postal county is refused with a 400 naming the postal
  county (`Coventry, Warwickshire` → West Midlands).
- A town outside the area named is refused with a 400 (`Maidstone, East Sussex`).

**Several places:** `Leeds; London` matches jobs in ANY of them, each within `distance_miles`, each job counted once.
A comma or `&` cannot separate places  -  `Leeds, London` is refused with a 400 asking for `;`.

**Home working:** `Remote`, `WFH`, `Work from home`, `Working from home` or `Home based` searches fully remote UK jobs,
on its own only  -  not in a `;` list, with `distance_miles` or with a `remote_working` other than `remote`. For remote
jobs in a place, send the place with `remote_working=remote`.

**Refusals** name what to send  -  never a silent search elsewhere: a shared name that is not the main place (candidates
listed), a name read as another place, or no such place (`UK`, `QQ9`). A real place with no matching job answers 0;
nationwide adverts can appear in any place search (`exclude_survey_jobs=true` drops the paid-survey ones).

**Echo:** `locations_resolved` lists each place (`query`, `location_id`, the `name` searched, and `exact_match`  -  `false`
when the text stood for it under another name); `location_resolved` is the first, null for home working.

`0` keeps jobs in the place itself. The website offers 0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 50; any whole number in the range works.
50 miles is the widest radius (a larger one returns exactly the 50-mile result, so it is refused).

Ex: `36` (Health & Medicine), `36,68` (Health & Medicine or Education), `52` (IT & Telecoms). Only the 38 top-level

**Salary floor, in pounds, in the unit set by `salary_unit` (annual by default).** Optional; `0` or more; pence allowed
(up to 2 decimal places, e.g. `12.21` with `salary_unit=hourly`).

Keeps jobs whose pay range REACHES the floor  -  the top of the range counts, so a £30,000 - £40,000 job passes
`min_salary=40000`. Pay is compared ANNUALISED, so hourly and daily-rate jobs are included on equal terms (a £500/day
contract passes `min_salary=40000`). Jobs that hide their pay ("Competitive salary") are matched on an undisclosed
figure the employer entered (not published: their `salary.from` / `to` are null), so some pass a floor their advert
does not show; add `salary_shown_only=true` to drop them. Ex: `30000`, `12.21` with `salary_unit=hourly`, or `500` with
`salary_unit=daily`.

max_salary.description:
**Salary ceiling, in pounds, in the unit set by `salary_unit`.** Optional; pence allowed (up to 2 decimal places). Must
not be below `min_salary`.

Keeps jobs whose pay range STARTS at or below the ceiling  -  the bottom of the range counts, so a £25,000 - £45,000 job
passes `max_salary=30000`. Compared on annualised pay like `min_salary`. Adverts that state no salary at all pass every
ceiling (add `salary_shown_only=true` to drop them). Ex: `25000`, or `12.50` with `salary_unit=hourly`.

salary_unit.description:
**The unit `min_salary` / `max_salary` are written in.** Optional; `annual` when omitted. Send it only with
`min_salary` or `max_salary`  -  on its own it is refused with a 400.

- `annual`  -  pounds per year (`30000`)
- `hourly`  -  pounds per hour (`15`; × 1,950 = 37.5 hours × 52 weeks, so `20` = `39000` a year)
- `daily`  -  pounds per day (`500`; × 260 working days, so `500` = `130000` a year)
- `weekly`  -  pounds per week (`1000`; × 52)
- `monthly`  -  pounds per month (`5000`; × 12)

The bounds are converted to annual pay with exactly these factors  -  `min_salary=20&salary_unit=hourly` returns the
same jobs as `min_salary=39000`. It changes how the bounds are read, not which jobs qualify by pay type: hourly,

parameters.name: location
parameters.description:
**Where the job is  -  a UK town, city, district, county, region, country or postcode, or up to 5 places separated by
`;`.** Optional; omit to search the whole UK.

Take the spelling from `/location-suggestions`; `/resolve-location` shows the exact place a text searches and explains
any refusal in full. Ex: `Leeds`, `Leeds; Manchester`, `SW1A 1AA`.

- **Other spellings** read as the listed place (`Herts` → "Hertfordshire"); a shared name is its main town (`Burton` →
  "Burton-on-Trent"); a postcode searches its outcode.
- **Town + area**, with or without the comma: a county, council area or nation narrows the town
  (`Leeds, West Yorkshire`, `Belfast, NI`); abbreviations and compass prefixes work (`Livingston, W Lothian`).
- **Postal county:** a town sent with a county other than its postal county is refused with a 400 naming the postal
  county (`Coventry, Warwickshire` → West Midlands).
- A town outside the area named is refused with a 400 (`Maidstone, East Sussex`).

**Several places:** `Leeds; London` matches jobs in ANY of them, each within `distance_miles`, each job counted once.
A comma or `&` cannot separate places  -  `Leeds, London` is refused with a 400 asking for `;`.

**Home working:** `Remote`, `WFH`, `Work from home`, `Working from home` or `Home based` searches fully remote UK jobs,
on its own only  -  not in a `;` list, with `distance_miles` or with a `remote_working` other than `remote`. For remote
jobs in a place, send the place with `remote_working=remote`.

**Refusals** name what to send  -  never a silent search elsewhere: a shared name that is not the main place (candidates
listed), a name read as another place, or no such place (`UK`, `QQ9`). A real place with no matching job answers 0;
nationwide adverts can appear in any place search (`exclude_survey_jobs=true` drops the paid-survey ones).

**Echo:** `locations_resolved` lists each place (`query`, `location_id`, the `name` searched, and `exact_match`  -  `false`
when the text stood for it under another name); `location_resolved` is the first, null for home working.

parameters.name: keywords
parameters.description:
**Free-text search over job titles and descriptions  -  the site's own search box.** Optional; omit to match every job.

**Matching:** Words separated by spaces must all match (`nurse midwife`); a comma means ANY of the terms (`nurse, midwife` returns jobs matching either); double quotes match an exact phrase (`"registered nurse"`).

**Exclusions & operators:** `-word` or `NOT word` excludes (`developer -java`); `-( … )` / `NOT ( … )` excludes a group (`nurse -(midwife OR doctor)`). `OR` / `|` / `/` / `and/or` means either word (`nurse OR midwife` = `nurse/midwife`); a `/` before an exclusion does not, so `tiler/-roofer` = `tiler -roofer`. `AND` requires both terms, and parentheses group expressions (`(developer OR engineer) AND python`).

**Wildcards & special characters:** `*` / `?` are wildcards (`develop*`). There are no boosts: `^` is read as a space (`nurse^2` searches `nurse 2`), and `%` is also read as a space (`100% remote` searches `100 remote`). Exception: a `%` between a word and a hyphen is dropped so the hyphen stays one (`20%-30%` = `20-30`, not `20 -30`).

**Other rules:** A value with no word at all  -  only punctuation or operators such as `,`, `|`, `OR`, `and/or`  -  is refused with a 400. A curly apostrophe is read as a straight one (`children’s nurse` = `children's nurse`).

**Examples:** `software developer`, `nurse, midwife`, `"data analyst"`, `developer -java`. **Up to 200 characters.**

description: Paste a reed.co.uk course page address and get the same course record /course-details returns.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description:
**A reed.co.uk course page address, pasted as-is** (`https://www.reed.co.uk/courses/{title}/{course_id}`). Required.

Only the id selects the course; the title part is cosmetic. A query string, `#fragment` and trailing slash are fine.

**Lenient pastes:** send `url` URL-encoded or not (unencoded query parts are read back into it). A missing
scheme, a `www.`, bare or `m.` host, quotes or a label around it, trailing punctuation, a Markdown, Slack or Jira link,
percent-encoding and text after the address are all read. The address ends at the first space, line break or `|`; a
line break that plainly cuts it is joined back.

**Refused with a 400** that names what to use instead:

- another site; a course listing (→ `/search-courses-by-url`), a job or company page;
- a bare number (→ `/course-details?course_id=…`);
- two different Reed addresses (the same one twice counts once), or an address broken off.
